Research scenarios only: probabilities are not a calibrated complete election forecast. No chamber-control probability is produced; the requested race list is incomplete.
Uncertainty floors and national/state correlation components are configurable sensitivity assumptions, not fitted 2026 parameters. More polls do not remove common polling error.

Bundled archive evaluation is a retrospective diagnostic, not an exact as-of replay: original publication availability is proxied and the historical archive selects eventual top-two candidates. Bundled historical coverage ends in 2022; it does not establish 2026 calibration.
Aggregate polling errors cannot identify which people switched or why; turnout, preference change and measurement error remain distinct explanations.
Empirical adjustments use only prior midterm cycles from the same chamber with an exact days-to-election horizon match and outcomes available by the cutoff.
Monte Carlo seed=20261101, draws=5000; maximum probability simulation standard error is approximately 0.007.
The API has no answer-party metadata; supplied primary candidate evidence is required for exact labels.
FEC candidate affiliation establishes a reported party, not ballot nomination certification.
Candidate-only rows are a research sensitivity input, not primary-reviewed current forecasting data.
Provider-created date is not a verified publication date; exact availability remains unobserved without a primary review.
Partisan/internal polls and ambiguous duplicate survey questions are excluded under this conservative QA policy.
The feed is an incomplete convenience sample of races and cannot justify chamber-control probabilities.
Every included sample count remains unverified; the engine uses placeholder n=1000 rather than claiming source subgroup n.
Some provider samples may refer to registered-voter totals rather than the reported likely-voter subset.
No pollster mode, likely-voter screen or weighting adjustment is inferred from an absent API field.
Current House geography follows the poll label; no previous-district baseline or map transfer is used.
Alaska ranked-choice races are excluded because first-choice D/R margins do not identify final-round outcomes.
Primary snapshot matching firm/contest/field windows take precedence over provider variants, including leaned-voter shares.
Archive available now is not a vintage dataset; historical publication dates are unknown.
Observation dates are median field dates, not publication dates or field end dates.
Candidates are the retrospectively selected top two election finishers; selection bias remains.
The provider has already imputed some sample sizes without a row-level imputation flag.
Historical actual margins are the archive's values; independent official-return reconciliation is not supplied.
This snapshot has no 2024 or 2026 election observations.
Publication lag and outcome availability lag are declared proxies, not observed release dates.
Archive map vintage is unknown; no district baseline or cross-map transfer is modeled.
November specials sharing the federal general-election date may remain as distinct race IDs.
Historical selection favors polled competitive D/R races and is not a representative chamber slate.
Baseline is the default: retrospective held-out evidence does not justify promoting a directional correction.
